summary: Added low-frequency, content-free Android log events to distinguish capture startup, Android-reported captured-content visibility, Android MediaProjection stop, and the app's normal capture teardown. Events contain no track IDs, account data, or captured content. These logs help separate app-only privacy masking from projection teardown during an authorized device reproduction; they do not identify why Android hid content or prove the stream reached a receiver.

checks.name: Android plugin unit tests and Java compilation
checks.observation: With the installed Homebrew JDK 17 selected explicitly, the WebRTC Android module unit tests and compileDebugJavaWithJavac both succeeded.

checks.name: Read-only Pixel projection and service state
checks.command: adb shell dumpsys media_projection; adb shell dumpsys activity services ru.boohtacord.app; adb shell pidof ru.boohtacord.app
checks.observation: ADB connected after an escalated read-only call. BOOHTACORD process was alive, Media Projection Manager returned null, and no BOOHTACORD foreground service was listed. This is only a point-in-time observation and does not identify why the capture ended. No app state was changed.

checks.name: Filtered MediaProjection system log
checks.observation: No retained events were available under the selected system tags; this does not establish the stop cause.

limitations: The plugin compiled, but runtime delivery of the Android 14 visibility callback and diagnostic log paths has not been observed on-device.

Although the user confirmed the Calculator capture was their test, the later read-only snapshot had no active MediaProjection or BOOHTACORD foreground service. No capture was started, stopped, or otherwise manipulated.
A device run is still needed to correlate visibility, projection stop, foreground service state, LiveKit publication, sender frames, receiver frames, and Mac rendering.
remaining: During a later authorized active capture, install a build containing these diagnostics and read filtered logs to correlate visibility and stop events with service, LiveKit publication, sender frames, receiver frames, and Mac rendering. Keep FE-59, FE-61 and FE-64 open until paired receiver playback and client-switch persistence pass.
